title: System Design: From First Principles to Interview Readiness
prerequisiteInterpretation: A required module is represented by its exit checkpoint; prior non-extension lessons are explicit within each module. This operational mapping is an authored interpretation of the source module-level skill requirements. L297–298 require either specialist branch and are omitted from the general route; they do not gate L299–300.

modules.title: Reasoning, requirements, and estimation
modules.prerequisiteText: Normal CS/programming fundamentals; no system-design prerequisite
modules.exitSkill: Turn an ambiguous request into scoped requirements, invariants, a workload model, and a timed design plan.

modules.title: The internet and communication protocols
modules.exitSkill: Trace a request, identify transport costs and trust boundaries, and select a communication protocol.

modules.title: Runtime behavior and API boundaries
modules.exitSkill: Design usable APIs and explain concurrency, overload, request cancellation, and service boundaries.

modules.title: Relational modeling and transactional correctness
modules.exitSkill: Derive schemas and indexes from access patterns and protect business invariants under concurrent writes.

modules.title: Storage engines and database selection
modules.exitSkill: Choose storage properties before products, including transactional, analytical, search, graph, and blob workloads.

modules.title: Measurement, scaling, and caching
modules.exitSkill: Scale a measured bottleneck and reason about cache correctness instead of adding infrastructure reflexively.

modules.title: Replication, partitioning, and identifiers
modules.exitSkill: Separate replication from sharding and handle skew, data movement, and identifier requirements.

modules.title: Consistency, partitions, and time
modules.exitSkill: Read distributed histories, choose precise guarantees, and explain what partitions and clocks make difficult.

modules.title: Consensus, coordination, and verification
modules.exitSkill: Explain replicated state machines, Raft fundamentals, and why leases need more than a timeout.

modules.title: Queues and reliable execution
modules.exitSkill: Build bounded, retry-safe asynchronous work with explicit acknowledgment and side-effect guarantees.

modules.title: Streams and cross-service transactions
modules.exitSkill: Locate transactional boundaries and reason about ordering, replay, and external effects in event pipelines.

modules.title: Data architecture and lifecycle
modules.exitSkill: Design derived views and data lifecycles without losing correctness during replay, change, or deletion.

modules.title: Reliability, observability, and disaster recovery
modules.exitSkill: Define user-facing reliability targets, investigate failures, and defend a recovery plan with measurable outcomes.

modules.title: Security, isolation, and admission control
modules.exitSkill: Place identity and authorization checks correctly and enforce tenant boundaries, quotas, and safe failure policies.

modules.title: Cloud infrastructure and safe evolution
modules.exitSkill: Map a design onto a deployment, explain control loops, and change software without violating data or availability contracts.

modules.title: Foundational complete designs
modules.exitSkill: Conduct full interviews for compact systems and defend caches, identifiers, limits, and failure behavior.

modules.title: Reusable backend and platform services
modules.exitSkill: Compose reliable backend primitives and distinguish scheduling, delivery, counting, and request routing.

modules.title: Chat, communities, and mail
modules.exitSkill: Design durable real-time communication and distinguish personal-chat, channel, and mailbox workloads.

modules.title: Social feeds and the first readiness gate
modules.exitSkill: Reason about fan-out and pagination, complete the chat project, and attempt mixed general-backend interviews.

modules.title: File synchronization and storage services
modules.exitSkill: Separate metadata from content and reason about synchronization, repair, durability, and cloud-storage control planes.

modules.title: Media delivery and content discovery
modules.exitSkill: Design separate upload/playback flows and support high-fan-out media, autocomplete, and crawling workloads.

modules.title: Location, marketplaces, and web search
modules.exitSkill: Design stateful marketplaces and spatial/search services under freshness, concurrency, and latency constraints.

modules.title: Correctness-critical and collaborative systems
modules.exitSkill: Defend business invariants and identity state despite retries, concurrent updates, and external dependencies.

modules.title: Logs, telemetry, and data-platform internals
modules.exitSkill: Design high-ingestion infrastructure and complete an event pipeline with demonstrable replay and migration behavior.

modules.title: Cloud control planes and advanced architecture
modules.exitSkill: Reason about fleet control, tenant placement, distributed counters, and safe long-lived architectural change.

modules.title: ML systems, feature stores, and recommendations
modules.exitSkill: Connect ML quality requirements to feature freshness, serving contracts, rollout safety, and measurable system behavior.

modules.title: LLM serving mechanics and capacity
modules.exitSkill: Estimate serving demand in tokens and memory, separate latency metrics, and reason about batching and GPU capacity.

modules.title: RAG and LLM application architecture
modules.exitSkill: Design retrieval and conversational applications with explicit quality, authorization, latency, and safety boundaries.

modules.title: ML operations, tool execution, and AI project
modules.exitSkill: Operate an AI gateway with versioned evaluation, controlled tool execution, and tested cost/failure behavior.

modules.title: Unseen interviews and final assessment
modules.exitSkill: Derive and defend unfamiliar architectures, respond to changed requirements, and document remaining skill gaps.
